# CaseAlerta — full reference

## OPT for F-1 students: DHS proposes a $70,000 fee (not in effect yet; comments due November 9)
Date: 2026-10-25 · URL: https://casealerta.com/en/news/proposed-opt-fee-70000-f1-students-comments-november-9-2026/

On October 8, 2026, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), through ICE, published a proposed rule in the Federal Register called "Optional Practical Training Fees."
OPT (Optional Practical Training) lets F-1 students work in their field of study.
## What it proposes, in plain words
- $70,000 per student the first time the school recommends OPT (before or after graduation).
- $30,000 for each later OPT recommendation, including the STEM OPT extension.
- The SEVP-certified school pays. The proposal does not stop the school from passing the cost to the student or employer.
- Payment would be due before the DSO (school official) enters the recommendation in SEVIS. Without payment, USCIS would not grant work authorization.
## Most important: it does not apply yet
- This is a proposal. It is not a final rule.
- Per the text, the fee would apply only to recommendations dated on or after the final rule's effective date, proposed as 60 days after the final rule is published.
- You do not have to pay anything new for your OPT today.
## Key dates
- Public comments: through November 9, 2026, at regulations.gov, docket ICEB-2026-0100.
- Comments on the information collection (Paperwork Reduction Act): through December 7, 2026.
- DHS will not consider comments sent by email, letter or hand delivery. Use the portal only.
## What to do
- Do not cancel or rush your OPT application out of fear. Talk to your school's DSO first.
- If you want to weigh in, comment at regulations.gov using ICEB-2026-0100 before November 9, 2026.
- If you already filed your Form I-765 for OPT, track it with your receipt number. CaseAlerta alerts you when it changes.
- Watch the Federal Register for a final rule and its effective date.
This is general information, not legal advice. For your case, talk to an immigration attorney or your school's DSO.

Sources: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/08/2026-20660/optional-practical-training-fees; https://iso.mit.edu/news/dhs-proposed-rule-to-establish-new-f-1-optional-practical-training-fees/

## USCIS Form I-797C (Notice of Action): what it means and what to do when you get one
Date: 2026-10-25 · URL: https://casealerta.com/en/news/form-i-797c-notice-of-action-what-it-means/

Form I-797C, Notice of Action, is a letter USCIS mails you to tell you something about your request.
## What USCIS uses it for
- Receipt: confirms USCIS received your request.
- Rejection: your package was not accepted (for example, missing fee or signature).
- Transfer: your case moved to another office.
- Reopening: USCIS reopened your case.
- Appointments: fingerprints or biometrics, interview, or a rescheduled appointment.
## What Form I-797C is NOT
- It is not an approval. USCIS says it is "only a receipt" proving you submitted your request.
- It does not give you status or a benefit. USCIS has not yet decided if you qualify.
- Some state, local, public or private agencies may accept it as supporting evidence for their own benefits.
## How to read it fast
- Look at the top for the notice type (for example, "Receipt Notice" or "Appointment Notice").
- Copy your receipt number: 3 letters and 10 digits. You use it to track your case.
- If it is an appointment, check the date, time and center address.
- If it is a rejection, read the reason before you file again.
## What to do
- Read and follow the instructions. USCIS warns that ignoring them might delay your case.
- Keep the original in a safe place and a digital copy. Older notices on sealed bond paper remain valid too.
- Add your receipt number to CaseAlerta to get an alert when your status changes.
- If you move, update your address with USCIS so you do not miss the next notice.
- To see how long your case may take, check USCIS's official processing times. They are ranges, not exact dates.
This is general information, not legal advice.

Sources: https://www.uscis.gov/forms/all-forms/form-i-797c-notice-of-action; https://egov.uscis.gov/processing-times/

## Ukraine and Sudan TPS after October 19, 2026: work permits remain valid for now
Date: 2026-10-24 · URL: https://casealerta.com/en/news/ukraine-sudan-tps-work-permit-after-october-19-2026/

Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Ukraine and Sudan was set to end on October 19, 2026.
On that same day, October 19, 2026, USCIS updated its official TPS pages for Ukraine and Sudan. It says an announcement for each country will be made "at the appropriate time."
Until then, according to USCIS, people from Ukraine and Sudan who are in the U.S. with TPS keep their protection, including work authorization.
## What it means in plain words
- Your TPS did not end on October 19. It stays in place until USCIS publishes a decision.
- You can keep working with your TPS work permit (EAD), categories A12 or C19.
- There is no new end date yet. There is also no new Federal Register notice extending or ending TPS for these countries.
## What we know and what is missing
- On August 14, 2026, USCIS posted employer notices (I-9 Central) that set the validity of these EADs through October 19, 2026.
- On October 19, USCIS said protection and work authorization continue until a new announcement.
- Formal Form I-9 guidance with a new date is still missing. Some employers may have questions when checking documents.
## What to do
- Save a printed or PDF copy of your country's TPS page on uscis.gov, with the date you checked it.
- If your employer asks, show them that page. Employer law firms recommend keeping it with the Form I-9.
- Do not stop working on your own before talking to your employer or a lawyer.
- Check the USCIS TPS page every week. The announcement can come at any time.
- If you have a pending EAD renewal, track it with your receipt number. CaseAlerta alerts you when it changes.
- If you have questions about your case, talk to an immigration lawyer or accredited representative. This is not legal advice.

Sources: https://www.uscis.gov/humanitarian/temporary-protected-status/TPS-Ukraine; https://www.uscis.gov/humanitarian/temporary-protected-status/temporary-protected-status-designated-country-sudan; https://www.uscis.gov/i-9-central/form-i-9-related-news/update-on-temporary-protected-status-for-ukraine-release-aug-14-2026; https://www.bal.com/immigration-news/united-states-sudan-ukraine-tps-beneficiaries-maintain-work-authorization-pending-further-uscis-guidance/

## November 2026 Visa Bulletin: EB-2 and EB-3 final action dates advance for the green card
Date: 2026-10-23 · URL: https://casealerta.com/en/news/visa-bulletin-november-2026/

The State Department published the November 2026 Visa Bulletin. In employment categories, EB-2 and EB-3 final action dates advance. Dates for Filing stay almost the same.
## Final action dates, employment (Rest of World and Mexico)
- EB-1: current.
- EB-2: April 1, 2025 (October was January 1, 2025).
- EB-3 professionals and skilled workers: June 15, 2024 (October was May 15, 2024).
- EB-3 other workers: June 1, 2022.
- EB-4: December 15, 2022.
- EB-5 unreserved: current.
## Dates for Filing, employment (Rest of World and Mexico)
- EB-2: March 15, 2026. EB-3: August 1, 2024. Other workers: July 1, 2022. EB-4: January 1, 2025.
- For November, employment-based adjustment of status (I-485) filings use the Dates for Filing chart. Confirm on the USCIS page before you file.
## Family: final action dates
- F1: Rest of World January 22, 2021; Mexico September 22, 2008.
- F2A: Rest of World October 22, 2026; Mexico April 22, 2026.
- F2B: Rest of World August 22, 2020; Mexico May 15, 2010.
- F3: Rest of World October 22, 2015; Mexico July 15, 2001.
- F4: Rest of World October 22, 2012; Mexico April 22, 2001.
## What to do
- Find your priority date on your I-797 notice (from the I-130 or I-140).
- If your date is earlier than the date in the chart USCIS names this month, you may prepare your I-485 with your attorney.
- Check the official chart every month: dates can move forward or back.
- This is general information, not legal advice.

Sources: https://travel.state.gov/content/dam/visas/Bulletins/visabulletin_November2026.pdf; https://www.uscis.gov/green-card/green-card-processes-and-procedures/visa-availability-priority-dates/when-to-file-your-adjustment-of-status-application-for-family-sponsored-or-employment-based-130; https://www.bal.com/immigration-news/united-states-november-2026-visa-bulletin-dates-for-filing-chart-applies-showing-no-movement-across-eb-categories/

## USCIS raises work permit, TPS, asylum and parole fees starting October 16, 2026
Date: 2026-10-22 · URL: https://casealerta.com/en/news/uscis-fee-increase-work-permit-tps-asylum-parole-october-2026/

USCIS adjusted some fees created by the H.R. 1 law for inflation. The notice ran in the Federal Register on October 1, 2026, and applies to anything postmarked on or after October 16, 2026.
This is not an increase to every fee. Only some asylum, TPS (Temporary Protected Status), parole and related work permit fees change.
## Fees that go up
- I-765, initial work permit (EAD) for asylum applicants: from $560 to $570.
- I-765, initial parole EAD: from $560 to $570.
- I-765, initial TPS EAD: from $560 to $570.
- I-821, TPS fee: from $510 to $520.
- I-589, annual pending asylum application fee: from $102 to $105.
- I-131, immigration parole fee: from $1,020 to $1,050.
## Fees that stay the same
- I-589, initial asylum fee: $100.
- Asylum EAD renewal or extension: $275.
- Parole or TPS EAD renewal or extension, and re-parole EAD: $280.
- I-360, Special Immigrant Juvenile (SIJ) fee: $250.
- I-94 fee: $24.
## Key point
- If your filing is postmarked October 16 or later and you pay the old amount, USCIS will reject it. You would have to file again.
- These amounts are only the H.R. 1 fee. Your form may carry other fees too.
## What to do
- Before you pay, check the exact amount in the official USCIS fee calculator and fee schedule (G-1055).
- If you already wrote a check or money order for the old amount, redo it.
- If you get rejected for the fee, refile with the right payment as soon as you can, especially if a deadline is close.
- Track your case with CaseAlerta to know when USCIS receives it.
This is general information, not legal advice. If your case is complex, talk to an immigration attorney.

Sources: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/10/01/2026-20187/fiscal-year-2027-inflation-adjustment-to-hr-1-immigration-fees; https://www.uscis.gov/newsroom/alerts/uscis-announces-fy-2027-inflation-increase-for-certain-immigration-related-fees; https://www.uscis.gov/g-1055

## USCIS changes filing deadlines that fall on a weekend or holiday starting October 23, 2026
Date: 2026-10-21 · URL: https://casealerta.com/en/news/uscis-filing-deadlines-weekend-holiday-october-23-2026/

USCIS updated its Policy Manual to clarify what happens when a filing deadline falls on a Saturday, Sunday or federal holiday. The alert is PA-2026-15, published September 23, 2026, and it applies starting October 23, 2026.
## What still moves to the next business day
- Deadlines counted in a number of days. For example, the 30 days to answer a Request for Evidence (RFE) or a Notice of Intent to Deny (NOID), or the deadline to file an appeal or motion.
- If the last day falls on a weekend or holiday, USCIS treats a filing received by the end of the next business day as on time.
## What NO LONGER moves to the next business day
- Deadlines that are not counted in days but depend on a fact: your age, the date your status expires, or another eligibility requirement.
- Example: if a child must file before turning 21 and the birthday is a Sunday, Monday is too late.
- Example: if your I-94 expires on a Saturday, the extension must be filed before it expires. Do not count on Monday.
- This reverses 2023 guidance that had moved these deadlines to the next business day.
## If you file online
- According to immigration attorneys' analysis, the next-business-day rule applies to paper filings. Online filings are treated as received when you submit them.
## What to do
- Check your dates: does your deadline depend on an age or on your status expiring? Then treat that day as the real limit and file earlier.
- If you mail it, leave extra days: what counts is the date USCIS RECEIVES it, not the date you send it.
- If you file online, do not wait until the last night.
- If an important deadline is near a weekend, talk to an attorney or accredited representative.
This is general information, not legal advice.

Sources: https://www.uscis.gov/sites/default/files/document/policy-manual-updates/20260923-DefinitionOfDay.pdf; https://www.uscis.gov/policy-manual/updates; https://www.rnlawgroup.com/uscis-changes-how-filing-deadlines-are-calculated-what-employers-and-foreign-workers-need-to-know/

## USCIS change of address (AR-11): how to do it online and not miss your mail
Date: 2026-10-20 · URL: https://casealerta.com/en/news/uscis-change-of-address-ar-11/

If you move, USCIS needs your new address. That is where it sends biometrics appointments, Requests for Evidence (RFE), interview notices and even your card. A wrong address can mean a missed appointment or a lost document.
## The basic rule
- Noncitizens in the U.S. must report a change of address to USCIS within 10 days of moving.
- If you have a pending case, report it as soon as possible.
- This does not apply to A and G visa holders or Visa Waiver Program visitors.
- USCIS does not list any fee for changing your address.
## How to do it online (the fastest way)
- Sign in to your USCIS online account and open the change-of-address tool from the account menu.
- Enter the receipt number of EACH pending case so USCIS updates the address on all of them.
- It works even if you filed your case by mail.
- If you change it online, do NOT also mail a paper Form AR-11.
## By mail
- You can also mail a paper Form AR-11 to the address listed on the form.
- Sign it: USCIS rejects unsigned AR-11 forms.
## The most common mistake
- Changing your address with the Postal Service (USPS) does NOT change it with USCIS, and USPS will not forward USCIS mail. Update both.
## Special cases
- If you sponsored someone with an affidavit of support, file Form I-865 within 30 days of your move.
- VAWA, T, U cases and I-751 abuse waivers have their own procedure. Check the official page before acting.
- If your case moved to the National Visa Center (NVC) or a consulate, also notify the Department of State.
## What to do
- If you moved in the last 10 days, change your address today in your USCIS account.
- Have all your receipt numbers ready.
- Save the confirmation.
- Keep tracking your cases for new notices. CaseAlerta alerts you when your status changes.
- If your situation is complex or you have an appointment coming up, talk to an immigration attorney. This is not legal advice.

Sources: https://www.uscis.gov/addresschange; https://www.uscis.gov/ar-11

## My USCIS case is not moving: is that normal? How to check processing times
Date: 2026-10-19 · URL: https://casealerta.com/en/news/my-uscis-case-is-not-moving-is-that-normal/

It is common for a case to go weeks or months without a status change. No movement does not mean there is a problem.
## How to know if you are on time
- Open the official USCIS processing times page.
- Choose your form (for example I-485 or I-765) and the office on your receipt notice.
- USCIS shows a range. If your case is past that range, you can submit an outside-normal-processing-time inquiry.
## What to do while you wait
- Keep your address updated with USCIS (Form AR-11 online).
- Answer any letter or RFE quickly.
- Turn on CaseAlerta alerts so you do not have to check every day: we tell you the moment it changes.

Sources: https://egov.uscis.gov/processing-times/; https://www.uscis.gov/addresschange

## USCIS receipt number: what the 3 letters mean (IOE, EAC, WAC, LIN, SRC, MSC)
Date: 2026-10-19 · URL: https://casealerta.com/en/news/uscis-receipt-number-prefixes-explained/

Your receipt number is on the I-797 notice USCIS sends when it receives your application. It has 13 characters: 3 letters and 10 digits.
## What the letters mean
- IOE: filed or processed online (USCIS electronic system).
- EAC: Vermont Service Center.
- WAC: California Service Center.
- LIN: Nebraska Service Center.
- SRC: Texas Service Center.
- MSC or NBC: National Benefits Center.
- YSC: Potomac Service Center.
## Tips
- Type it without dashes or spaces, for example IOE0912345678.
- If your case is transferred, the receipt number does NOT change.
- Keep the I-797 notice: it proves USCIS received your case.

Sources: https://egov.uscis.gov/; https://www.uscis.gov/forms/filing-guidance/form-i-797-types-and-functions

## I got an RFE from USCIS: what it is and what to do, step by step
Date: 2026-10-19 · URL: https://casealerta.com/en/news/got-an-rfe-from-uscis-what-to-do/

If your status says "Request for Additional Evidence Was Sent", USCIS will mail you a letter called an RFE. It is not a denial: they need more proof to decide.
## Step by step
- Wait for the paper letter and read it fully. It lists exactly what they need and the deadline.
- List each item and gather one document for each.
- Put the RFE page on top of your package, as the letter asks.
- Send EVERYTHING in one package, before the deadline, to the address in the letter.
- Keep copies of everything and a tracked mailing receipt.
## After you send it
- When USCIS receives it, your status will change to "Response To USCIS' Request For Evidence Was Received".
- If the RFE is complex, talk to an immigration attorney before answering.

Sources: https://www.uscis.gov/policy-manual/volume-1-part-e-chapter-6

## USCIS finalizes the end of the 540-day automatic EAD extension
Date: 2026-10-14 · URL: https://casealerta.com/en/news/ead-automatic-extension-ends/

On October 14, 2026 the Federal Register published a final rule adopting, without changes, the interim rule on employment authorization documents (EAD, Form I-766). It took effect the same day.
## What changed
- The up-to-540-day automatic extension only applies to renewals filed BEFORE October 30, 2025.
- If you filed your renewal on or after October 30, 2025, your EAD expires on the printed date unless a law, regulation or Federal Register notice says otherwise.
- Extensions tied to TPS (Temporary Protected Status) and others provided by law or notice are not affected.
## What to do
- Check the expiration date on your EAD card today.
- File your renewal as early as possible: USCIS allows filing up to 180 days before expiration.
- Track your renewal case so you know the moment it is approved. CaseAlerta alerts you by push and email.
- If your job depends on your EAD, talk to your employer and, if in doubt, an immigration attorney.

Sources: https://www.federalregister.gov/d/2026-20955; https://www.uscis.gov/i-765

## USCIS proposes ending deference to prior approvals for work visa extensions
Date: 2026-10-14 · URL: https://casealerta.com/en/news/uscis-proposes-ending-deference-extensions/

On October 14, 2026 USCIS published a proposed rule that would remove 8 CFR 214.1(c)(5). Today that policy lets officers give weight to a prior approval when the facts have not changed.
## What it would mean
- Every extension of a work petition or stay (for example H-1B or L-1) would be reviewed as if it were new.
- The petitioner or applicant must prove eligibility again in full.
- It is a proposal: it is not in effect yet.
## What to do
- Employers: prepare complete extension packages, as if filing for the first time.
- Anyone can comment at regulations.gov until November 13, 2026.
- If your extension is pending, track it with CaseAlerta so you can answer fast if USCIS sends a Request for Evidence (RFE).

Sources: https://www.federalregister.gov/d/2026-20941; https://www.regulations.gov/

## October 2026 Visa Bulletin: EB-2 moves forward strongly for Rest of World
Date: 2026-09-29 · URL: https://casealerta.com/en/news/visa-bulletin-october-2026/

The October 2026 Visa Bulletin opens fiscal year 2027. USCIS stated that employment-based cases use the Dates for Filing chart.
## Dates for Filing, employment (Rest of World, includes Mexico)
- EB-1: current.
- EB-2: March 15, 2026.
- EB-3 professionals and skilled workers: August 1, 2024.
- EB-3 other workers: June 1, 2022.
- EB-4: January 1, 2025.
- EB-5 unreserved: current.
## What to do
- Compare your priority date (on your I-140 or I-130 I-797 notice) with the chart.
- If your date is earlier than the bulletin date, you may prepare your adjustment of status (I-485) with your attorney.
- Always confirm dates in the official State Department bulletin: they change every month.

Sources: https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/legal/visa-law0/visa-bulletin.html; https://www.uscis.gov/green-card/green-card-processes-and-procedures/visa-availability-priority-dates/adjustment-of-status-filing-charts-from-the-visa-bulletin; https://www.envoyglobal.com/news-alert/october-2026-visa-bulletin/
